source.text: כִּי֩ יְרַחֵ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֗ב וּבָחַ֥ר עוֹד֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהִנִּיחָ֖ם עַל־אַדְמָתָ֑ם וְנִלְוָ֤ה הַגֵּר֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְנִסְפְּח֖וּ עַל־בֵּ֥ית יַעֲקֹֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: For will have compassion Yahweh on Jacob, and he will choose again Israel, and he will give them rest on their land, and will join himself the sojourner to them, and they will attach themselves to [the] house of Jacob.

en.L: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will have compassion on Jacob and will choose Israel again, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give them rest on their land; and the sojourner will join himself to them, and they will attach themselves to the house of Jacob.
en.B: Yes, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will show mercy to Jacob. He will choose Israel once more and let them settle in peace on their own soil. The foreigner living among them will join them, and such people will bind themselves to the house of Jacob.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will be kind to the people of Jacob again. He will choose Israel once more and let them live in peace in their own land. Foreigners will join them and become part of the family of Jacob.

decisions.choice: for: the promise that follows explains the fall of Babylon in chapter 13
decisions.reason: The word ties this chapter to the oracle against Babylon in chapter 13: Babylon will fall because God will have compassion on his people and bring them home.

decisions.choice: give them rest: settle them securely
decisions.reason: The verb means to set someone down at rest, settled and secure. The same root returns in verses 3 and 7: Israel is given rest, and then the whole earth is at rest.

decisions.choice: the sojourner: a foreigner living among Israel
decisions.reason: The word is used of a resident alien, someone from another people living in Israel's land (Exodus 22:20; Leviticus 19:34). Here such people choose to belong to Israel (compare 56:3-7).

decisions.choice: the people of Jacob / the family of Jacob
decisions.reason: Jacob is the name of the people descended from him; Readable says so. Literal and Balanced keep "Jacob" and "the house of Jacob".

source.text: וּלְקָח֣וּם עַמִּים֮ וֶהֱבִיא֣וּם אֶל־מְקוֹמָם֒ וְהִֽתְנַחֲל֣וּם בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עַ֚ל אַדְמַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה לַעֲבָדִ֖ים וְלִשְׁפָח֑וֹת וְהָיוּ֙ שֹׁבִ֣ים לְשֹֽׁבֵיהֶ֔ם וְרָד֖וּ בְּנֹגְשֵׂיהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And will take them peoples and will bring them to their place, and will possess them [the] house of Israel on [the] land of Yahweh as male servants and as female servants, and they will be taking captive their captors and they will rule over their oppressors.

en.L: And peoples will take them and bring them to their place, and the house of Israel will possess them on the land of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as male servants and as female servants; and they will take captive those who took them captive, and they will rule over their oppressors.
en.B: Peoples will take them and bring them home, and the house of Israel will hold those peoples as their own, male and female servants on the land of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Those who once carried them off will become their captives, and they will rule over those who oppressed them.
en.R: Other nations will take the people of Israel and bring them back home. Then Israel will have people from those nations as their servants, both men and women, in the land that belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Israel will capture those who had captured them. They will rule over those who had been cruel to them.

decisions.choice: possess them: take them as an inheritance
decisions.reason: The verb means to take as one's own lasting property, used of receiving the land as an inheritance. Here the peoples who once held Israel become Israel's possession.

decisions.choice: a reversal: captors become captives, oppressors are ruled
decisions.reason: The roles of exile are turned around. The words for oppressors and ruling return in verses 4-6 of the king of Babylon, whose rule is broken.

decisions.choice: the land of Yahweh: the land of Israel as belonging to God
decisions.reason: Israel's land belongs to Yahweh (Leviticus 25:23; Hosea 9:3); the people live on it as his tenants.

decisions.choice: Other nations will take the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable names who "them" are, as verse 1 shows.

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ מֵֽעָצְבְּךָ֖ וּמֵרָגְזֶ֑ךָ וּמִן־הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה הַקָּשָׁ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֻבַּד־בָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be on [the] day gives rest Yahweh to you from your pain and from your turmoil and from the labor the hard which was labored by you,

en.L: And it will be, on the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives you rest from your pain and from your turmoil and from the hard labor that was laid on you,
en.B: And on the day when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives you rest from your sorrow and your unrest, and from the cruel bondage forced on you,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will give you rest from your pain and trouble. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will free you from the hard work that you were forced to do in bondage. When that day comes,

decisions.choice: the hard labor: the language of slavery in Egypt
decisions.reason: "Hard labor" is the phrase used of Israel's forced work in Egypt (Exodus 1:14; 6:9; Deuteronomy 26:6). Release from Babylon is pictured as a new exodus.

decisions.choice: you: Israel, addressed as one person
decisions.reason: The pronoun is singular: the people are spoken to as one. The same "you" takes up the taunt in verse 4.

decisions.choice: it will be on the day: the sentence continues into verse 4
decisions.reason: The time clause sets the scene for what Israel will do in verse 4.

decisions.choice: When that day comes,
decisions.reason: Readable states the promise first in short sentences and moves the time clause to the end, where it leads into verse 4.

decisions.choice: bondage
decisions.reason: "Bondage" in Balanced and Readable for the hard labor, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps the echo of slavery in Egypt.

source.text: וְנָשָׂ֜אתָ הַמָּשָׁ֥ל הַזֶּ֛ה עַל־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל וְאָמָ֑רְתָּ אֵ֚יךְ שָׁבַ֣ת נֹגֵ֔שׂ שָׁבְתָ֖ה מַדְהֵבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and you will lift up this saying against [the] king of Babylon and you will say, how has ceased [the] oppressor, has ceased [the] raging!

en.L: that you will lift up this taunt against the king of Babylon and say: \q How the oppressor has ceased, \q [how the] raging has ceased!
en.B: you will sing this mocking song about the king of Babylon: \q How still the oppressor has become! \q How his raging has come to an end!
en.R: you will sing this song to make fun of the king of Babylon: \q The cruel ruler is finished! \q His fury has stopped!

decisions.choice: this saying: a taunt, a song of mockery
decisions.reason: The word is used of a proverb or comparison, and also of a mocking song sung over a fallen enemy (Micah 2:4; Habakkuk 2:6). What follows (verses 4-21) is a funeral song turned into mockery.

decisions.choice: raging: an onslaught, a fury that drives others
alternatives: golden city (a guess at the traditional Hebrew word)
decisions.reason: The traditional Hebrew text has a word found nowhere else, of unknown meaning (once guessed to mean "golden city"). The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) has a word differing by one letter that means onslaught or raging, and the Septuagint's rendering points to the same sense. This translation follows that reading.

decisions.choice: the king of Babylon: the ruler of the empire whose fall chapter 13 announced
decisions.reason: The song is about the king of Babylon as the embodiment of that empire. The king is not named; the oracle reaches past any one reign.

decisions.choice: mocking song / song to make fun of
decisions.reason: Literal says "taunt"; Balanced and Readable say what kind of song it is.

source.text: שָׁבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה מַטֵּ֣ה רְשָׁעִ֑ים שֵׁ֖בֶט מֹשְׁלִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Has broken Yahweh [the] staff of [the] wicked, [the] scepter of rulers,

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has broken the staff of the wicked, \q the scepter of rulers,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has snapped the rod of the wicked, \q the scepter held by tyrants,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has broken the power of the wicked. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has broken the scepter of evil rulers,

decisions.choice: staff, scepter: the rod of rule, standing for power to strike
decisions.reason: The staff and scepter are the ruler's rod, used to rule and to beat (verse 6). Assyria was the rod of God's anger in 10:5; now the rod of Babylon is broken.

decisions.choice: has broken: the song speaks of the fall as already done
decisions.reason: The song is sung looking back on Babylon's fall, so its verbs speak of it as past.

decisions.choice: the power of the wicked
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the staff.

source.text: מַכֶּ֤ה עַמִּים֙ בְּעֶבְרָ֔ה מַכַּ֖ת בִּלְתִּ֣י סָרָ֑ה רֹדֶ֤ה בָאַף֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם מֻרְדָּ֖ף בְּלִ֥י חָשָֽׂךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [which] struck peoples in wrath, a blow not ceasing, [which] ruled in anger nations, persecution not [anyone] restrained.

en.L: which struck peoples in wrath, \q a blow without ceasing, \q which ruled nations in anger, \q a persecution [that] none restrained.
en.B: the rod that beat the peoples in fury with blow after blow that never let up, \q that ruled the nations in anger \q and hunted them down with no one to hold it back.
en.R: That ruler was angry and kept on beating the peoples of the world. He never stopped. \q In his anger he ruled over the nations. \q He chased them down, and no one could stop him.

decisions.choice: persecution: pursuit, hounding
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "pursue" and pictures the empire chasing down the nations it ruled.

decisions.choice: struck, ruled: describing the staff and scepter of verse 5
decisions.reason: The two participles describe the rod of verse 5, and through it the power that held it.

decisions.choice: none restrained: no one held it back
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean that no one restrained the persecutor, or that the persecution was unsparing. The sense is the same: it went on unchecked.

decisions.choice: That ruler
decisions.reason: Readable says who used the rod, as verse 5 implies.

source.text: נָ֥חָה שָׁקְטָ֖ה כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ פָּצְח֖וּ רִנָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Is at rest, is at peace all the earth; they have broken forth [into] a shout of joy.

en.L: All the earth is at rest, is quiet; \q they have broken forth [into] a shout of joy.
en.B: Now all the earth lies still and calm; \q people burst out in shouts of joy.
en.R: Now the whole world is resting and peaceful. \q People are shouting for joy.

decisions.choice: at rest, quiet: free from war and oppression
decisions.reason: The first verb is the root of "rest" in verses 1 and 3; the second is used of a land at peace after war (Judges 3:11; 5:31). The rest given to Israel spreads to the whole earth.

decisions.choice: they have broken forth: the earth's peoples
decisions.reason: The plural verb has the earth's people as its subject.

source.text: גַּם־בְּרוֹשִׁ֛ים שָׂמְח֥וּ לְךָ֖ אַרְזֵ֣י לְבָנ֑וֹן מֵאָ֣ז שָׁכַ֔בְתָּ לֹֽא־יַעֲלֶ֥ה הַכֹּרֵ֖ת עָלֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Also [the] junipers have rejoiced over you, [the] cedars of Lebanon: from then you lay down, not comes up the cutter against us.

en.L: Even the junipers rejoice over you, the cedars of Lebanon: \q "Since you lay down, the cutter does not come up against us."
en.B: Even the junipers and the cedars of Lebanon are glad over you: \q "Ever since you lay down, no one climbs up here to chop us down."
en.R: Even the juniper trees and the cedars of Lebanon are happy about what happened to you. \q They say, "Since you died, no one comes up here to cut us down."

decisions.choice: the cedars of Lebanon: forests stripped by conquering kings
decisions.reason: Kings of the great empires cut timber in Lebanon for their buildings and their wars; Isaiah 37:24 has the king of Assyria boast of it, and Habakkuk 2:17 speaks of violence done to Lebanon. Now the trees are safe.

decisions.choice: junipers: a tall evergreen of Lebanon
decisions.reason: The tree cannot be named with certainty; it is a large evergreen used for building, perhaps a juniper, cypress or fir.

decisions.choice: you lay down: you died
decisions.reason: "Lie down" is used of death and burial (verse 18; 1 Kings 2:10).

decisions.choice: They say
decisions.reason: Readable marks the start of the trees' words, which the Hebrew gives without a verb of speaking.

decisions.choice: Since you died
decisions.reason: Readable says what "lay down" means here.

source.text: שְׁא֗וֹל מִתַּ֛חַת רָגְזָ֥ה לְךָ֖ לִקְרַ֣את בּוֹאֶ֑ךָ עוֹרֵ֨ר לְךָ֤ רְפָאִים֙ כָּל־עַתּ֣וּדֵי אָ֔רֶץ הֵקִים֙ מִכִּסְאוֹתָ֔ם כֹּ֖ל מַלְכֵ֥י גוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Sheol from beneath is excited over you, to meet your coming; it has roused for you [the] shades, all [the] leaders of [the] earth; it has made rise from their thrones all [the] kings of [the] nations.

en.L: Sheol from beneath is stirred up over you to meet your coming; \q it rouses for you the shades, all the he-goats of the earth; \q it raises from their thrones all the kings of the nations.
en.B: Down below, Sheol is astir because of you, waiting to meet you as you arrive. \q It wakes the dead for your sake, all who once led the earth; \q it makes every king of the nations rise from his throne.
en.R: Down below, the grave is excited about you. It is getting ready to meet you when you come. \q It wakes up the dead to greet you, all who were once leaders on the earth. \q It makes the kings of all the nations stand up from their thrones.

decisions.choice: Sheol: the world of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place below where all the dead were pictured as gathered. In this song it is a vast hall where the dead kings sit on their thrones.

decisions.choice: shades: the weak, shadowy dead
decisions.reason: The word is used of the dead in Sheol (26:14, 19; Psalm 88:11; Proverbs 9:18). It describes them as strengthless, as verse 10 says.

decisions.choice: he-goats: leaders
decisions.reason: The leaders are called "he-goats", the male goats that go at the head of a flock (Jeremiah 50:8; Zechariah 10:3).

decisions.choice: the grave
decisions.reason: Readable says "the grave" for Sheol, the world of the dead; Literal and Balanced keep the name.

decisions.choice: the dead
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "shades", the word for the weak, shadowy dead; Balanced and Readable say "the dead".

decisions.choice: all who once led the earth / all who were once leaders
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "he-goats"; Balanced and Readable say what the picture means.

source.text: כֻּלָּ֣ם יַֽעֲנ֔וּ וְיֹאמְר֖וּ אֵלֶ֑יךָ גַּם־אַתָּ֛ה חֻלֵּ֥יתָ כָמ֖וֹנוּ אֵלֵ֥ינוּ נִמְשָֽׁלְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: All of them will answer and will say to you, also you have been made weak like us, to us you have become like.

en.L: All of them will answer and say to you, \q "You too have been made weak as we [are]; you have become like us."
en.B: They will all speak up and say to you, \q "So you too have been brought low, as weak as we are! Now you are one of us!"
en.R: All of them will say to you, \q "Now you are weak, just like us! You have become one of us!"

decisions.choice: you too: even you, the mighty king
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stressed: even the king who ruled the nations is now as powerless as the dead he once sent there.

decisions.choice: the end of the shades' words
decisions.reason: The words of the dead may end here or run on through verse 11. Either way verse 11 continues the mockery; this translation closes their words at the end of verse 10.

source.text: הוּרַ֥ד שְׁא֛וֹל גְּאוֹנֶ֖ךָ הֶמְיַ֣ת נְבָלֶ֑יךָ תַּחְתֶּ֨יךָ֙ יֻצַּ֣ע רִמָּ֔ה וּמְכַסֶּ֖יךָ תּוֹלֵעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Has been brought down [to] Sheol your pride, [the] sound of your harps; under you is spread maggots, and your coverings [are] worms.

en.L: Your pride has been brought down [to] Sheol, the sound of your harps; \q beneath you maggots are spread [as a bed], and worms [are] your covering.
en.B: Your splendor has gone down to Sheol, along with the music of your harps. \q Under you a mattress of maggots is spread, and worms are your blanket.
en.R: All your proud glory has been brought down to the grave, along with the music of your harps. \q Now you lie on a bed of maggots, and worms are spread over you like a blanket.

decisions.choice: pride: majesty, grandeur, with a hint of arrogance
decisions.reason: The word means height or majesty, and often pride (2:10, 19; 13:11, 19). It names both the king's splendor and his arrogance.

decisions.choice: maggots and worms: a bed and blanket for the corpse
decisions.reason: A king lay on a fine couch under rich coverings; now his bed and covering are the worms that eat the body (compare Job 17:14).

decisions.choice: the grave
decisions.reason: Readable says "the grave" for Sheol, the world of the dead; Literal and Balanced keep the name.

source.text: אֵ֛יךְ נָפַ֥לְתָּ מִשָּׁמַ֖יִם הֵילֵ֣ל בֶּן־שָׁ֑חַר נִגְדַּ֣עְתָּ לָאָ֔רֶץ חוֹלֵ֖שׁ עַל־גּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: How you have fallen from heaven, shining one, son of dawn! You have been cut down to [the] ground, [you who] defeated nations!

en.L: How you have fallen from heaven, shining one, son of dawn! \q You have been cut down to the ground, [you who] weakened nations!
en.B: How you have fallen from the heavens, shining one, son of Dawn! \q You have been hewn down to the earth, you who brought the nations to their knees!
en.R: You were like the bright morning star, but now you have fallen from the sky! \q You once defeated nations, but now you have been chopped down to the ground!

decisions.choice: shining one, son of dawn: the morning star, a title for the king of Babylon
decisions.reason: The name comes from the verb "shine" and most likely means the bright morning star (the planet Venus), which rises before dawn and fades as the sun climbs. The proud king who rose so high is pictured as that star, cast down. The Septuagint has "the morning star" here, and the Latin Vulgate has "Lucifer", the Latin name of the morning star ("light-bearer"), a name kept in the King James Version. Later Christian readers often applied the verse to the fall of Satan (compare Luke 10:18), and "Lucifer" became a name for Satan; in Isaiah the song is sung over the king of Babylon (verse 4).

decisions.choice: weakened nations: overpowered them, laid them low
decisions.reason: The verb means to overpower or make weak (Exodus 17:13). The word for the king's own fall ("made weak") came in verse 10.

decisions.choice: fallen, cut down: a star falling and a tree felled
decisions.reason: Two pictures meet: the star falls from the sky, and the king is cut down like the trees he once cut (verse 8; 10:33-34).

decisions.choice: You were like the bright morning star
decisions.reason: Readable names the star and makes the comparison plain; Literal and Balanced keep the title "shining one".

source.text: וְאַתָּ֞ה אָמַ֤רְתָּ בִֽלְבָבְךָ֙ הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם אֶֽעֱלֶ֔ה מִמַּ֥עַל לְכֽוֹכְבֵי־אֵ֖ל אָרִ֣ים כִּסְאִ֑י וְאֵשֵׁ֥ב בְּהַר־מוֹעֵ֖ד בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֥י צָפֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And you said in your heart, the heavens I will ascend, above to [the] stars of El I will raise my throne, and I will sit on [the] mountain of assembly in [the] remotest parts of Zaphon.

en.L: And you said in your heart, "[To] the heavens I will ascend; \q above the stars of God I will raise my throne; \q and I will sit on the mountain of assembly in the remotest parts of Zaphon.
en.B: In your heart you said, "I will climb into the heavens \q and lift my throne higher than the stars of God. \q I will take my seat on the mountain where the assembly meets, in the far heights of Zaphon.
en.R: You said to yourself, "I will go up to heaven. \q I will put my throne higher than God's stars. \q I will sit as king on the mountain where the heavenly council meets, far away in the north.

decisions.choice: the stars of El: the stars of God, the heavenly host
decisions.reason: El is the common word for God. The stars stand for the highest heavenly beings (Job 38:7); the king wants his throne above them all.

decisions.choice: the mountain of assembly in the far reaches of Zaphon: the mountain of the heavenly council
alternatives: the far reaches of the north
decisions.reason: Zaphon means "north" and was also the name of a high mountain north of Israel, pictured by Israel's neighbors as the home of their gods. Psalm 48:3 gives the phrase "the far reaches of Zaphon" to Mount Zion, God's true dwelling, and Psalm 82:1 speaks of God standing in the divine assembly. The king claims a seat where only God rules.

decisions.choice: you said in your heart: you thought to yourself
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is the seat of thought and plans. The king's boast, five times "I will", runs into verse 14.

decisions.choice: the mountain where the heavenly council meets, far away in the north
decisions.reason: Readable explains the mountain of assembly and translates the name Zaphon by its meaning, "north".

source.text: אֶעֱלֶ֖ה עַל־בָּ֣מֳתֵי עָ֑ב אֶדַּמֶּ֖ה לְעֶלְיֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: I will ascend above [the] high places of [the] cloud; I will make myself like the Most High.

en.L: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; \q I will make myself like the Most High."
en.B: I will rise higher than the cloud tops; \q I will make myself the equal of the Most High."
en.R: I will go up above the highest clouds. \q I will be just like God Most High."

decisions.choice: the Most High: a title of God
decisions.reason: The title names God as supreme over all (Genesis 14:19; Psalm 47:3). The king wants to be his rival.

decisions.choice: I will make myself like: make myself equal to
decisions.reason: The verb form is reflexive: the king makes himself like God. The same root asks "to whom will you liken God?" in 40:18, 25 and 46:5.

decisions.choice: God Most High
decisions.reason: Readable says "God" so that the title is clear (Genesis 14:18).

source.text: אַ֧ךְ אֶל־שְׁא֛וֹל תּוּרָ֖ד אֶל־יַרְכְּתֵי־בֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: Nevertheless to Sheol you have been brought down, to [the] remotest parts of [the] pit.

en.L: But to Sheol you are brought down, to the remotest parts of the pit.
en.B: Instead you are dragged down to Sheol, into the deepest corners of the pit.
en.R: But instead you have been brought down to the grave, to the deepest part of the pit.

decisions.choice: the remotest parts: the same words as "the far reaches of Zaphon"
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats the word used in verse 13: the king aimed at the farthest heights of the north and reaches the farthest depths of the pit.

decisions.choice: the pit: the grave, the world of the dead
decisions.reason: The word means a cistern or pit and is used of the grave and of Sheol (38:18; Psalm 28:1).

decisions.choice: the grave
decisions.reason: Readable says "the grave" for Sheol, the world of the dead; Literal and Balanced keep the name.

source.text: רֹאֶ֨יךָ֙ אֵלֶ֣יךָ יַשְׁגִּ֔יחוּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ יִתְבּוֹנָ֑נוּ הֲזֶ֤ה הָאִישׁ֙ מַרְגִּ֣יז הָאָ֔רֶץ מַרְעִ֖ישׁ מַמְלָכֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Those who see you at you will stare, at you they will consider carefully: [is] this the man [who] made tremble the earth, [who] made shake kingdoms,

en.L: Those who see you will stare at you; they will look closely at you: \q "Is this the man who made the earth tremble, \q who made kingdoms shake,
en.B: All who see you will gaze at you and look you over closely: \q "Can this be the man who set the earth trembling \q and made kingdoms quake,
en.R: People who see you will stare at you. \q They will look at you closely and ask, "Is this really the man who made the earth tremble? \q Is this the one who shook kingdoms with fear?

decisions.choice: those who see you: onlookers at the king's unburied body
decisions.reason: The scene moves from the world of the dead back to the earth, where people look at the king's body thrown out unburied (verse 19).

decisions.choice: made tremble, made shake: made the world shudder with fear
decisions.reason: Both verbs are used of the earth quaking. The king who made the earth shake is now an object of stares.

decisions.choice: Is this really the man ... ? Is this the one ... ?
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long question into two and repeats the question.

source.text: שָׂ֥ם תֵּבֵ֛ל כַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר וְעָרָ֣יו הָרָ֑ס אֲסִירָ֖יו לֹא־פָ֥תַח בָּֽיְתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: [who] made [the] world like the wilderness and its cities tore down, his prisoners not opened homeward?

en.L: who made the world like a wilderness and tore down its cities, \q [who] did not let his prisoners [go] home?"
en.B: who turned the world into a wasteland and pulled down its cities, \q who never set his prisoners free to go home?"
en.R: He turned the world into a desert. He destroyed its cities. \q He never let his prisoners go home."

decisions.choice: did not open homeward for his prisoners: kept captives in exile
decisions.reason: Empires deported conquered peoples and did not let them return (2 Kings 17:6; 25:11). This was Israel's own experience, now ended (verses 1-2).

decisions.choice: like the wilderness: an empty, desolate land
decisions.reason: The wilderness is uninhabited land. The king's wars left the world as empty as a desert.

decisions.choice: He turned ... He destroyed ... He never let ...
decisions.reason: Readable continues the onlookers' words as statements after the question of verse 16.

source.text: כָּל־מַלְכֵ֥י גוֹיִ֖ם כֻּלָּ֑ם שָׁכְב֥וּ בְכָב֖וֹד אִ֥ישׁ בְּבֵיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: All [the] kings of [the] nations, all of them, have lain down in glory, each in his house,

en.L: All the kings of the nations, all of them, \q lie in glory, each in his [own] house,
en.B: Every king of the nations, every one of them, \q lies at rest with honor, each in a tomb of his own,
en.R: All the other kings of the nations lie with honor in their own graves.

decisions.choice: his house: his tomb
decisions.reason: A tomb could be called a house, a lasting home (Job 17:13; Ecclesiastes 12:5). Each dead king lies in his own tomb.

decisions.choice: in glory: with honor, in a fitting burial
decisions.reason: Kings were buried with honor in royal tombs. The contrast in verse 19 is a king left without a grave.

decisions.choice: graves
decisions.reason: Readable says what "house" means here.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֞ה הָשְׁלַ֤כְתָּ מִֽקִּבְרְךָ֙ כְּנֵ֣צֶר נִתְעָ֔ב לְב֥וּשׁ הֲרֻגִ֖ים מְטֹ֣עֲנֵי חָ֑רֶב יוֹרְדֵ֥י אֶל־אַבְנֵי־ב֖וֹר כְּפֶ֥גֶר מוּבָֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: And you have been thrown out from your tomb like a shoot abhorred, [the] clothing of [the] slain, pierced of [the] sword, those going down to [the] stones of [the] pit, like a corpse trodden down.

en.L: But you have been thrown out from your tomb like an abhorred shoot, \q [with the] clothing of [the] slain, pierced by the sword, \q who go down to the stones of the pit, like a trampled corpse.
en.B: But you have been flung away from your grave like a branch nobody wants, \q dressed in the bodies of the slain, of those run through by the sword, \q who sink down to the stones of the pit, like a corpse that feet have trampled.
en.R: But you have been thrown out of your grave, like a branch that someone hates and throws away. \q You are covered with the bodies of soldiers killed by the sword, who have gone down to the rocky pit. \q You are like a dead body that people walk on.

decisions.choice: an abhorred shoot: a worthless branch thrown away
decisions.reason: A shoot is a branch growing from a root; the word is used of the shoot from Jesse in 11:1. This shoot is loathed and cast aside. The Septuagint has "like a loathsome corpse" here.

decisions.choice: the clothing of the slain: covered with dead bodies
decisions.reason: The king lies under the bodies of the battle dead as if they were his clothing, instead of a royal shroud.

decisions.choice: the stones of the pit: the bottom of the grave
alternatives: the stones heaped over a grave
decisions.reason: The pit is the grave (verse 15); its stones may be the stones of a burial pit or a mass grave.

decisions.choice: soldiers killed by the sword
decisions.reason: Readable says that the slain are those killed in battle, as the next phrase implies.

source.text: לֹֽא־תֵחַ֤ד אִתָּם֙ בִּקְבוּרָ֔ה כִּֽי־אַרְצְךָ֥ שִׁחַ֖תָּ עַמְּךָ֣ הָרָ֑גְתָּ לֹֽא־יִקָּרֵ֥א לְעוֹלָ֖ם זֶ֥רַע מְרֵעִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you will be united with them in burial, for your land you have ruined, your people you have slain; not will be named forever [the] offspring of evildoers.

en.L: You will not be joined with them in burial, \q for you have ruined your land, you have slain your people. \q Not forever will the offspring of evildoers be named.
en.B: You will have no share with them in a grave, \q because you ruined your own land and put your own people to death. \q The descendants of evildoers will never again be spoken of.
en.R: You will not be buried like the other kings, \q because you destroyed your own land and killed your own people. \q The children of evil people will never be remembered.

decisions.choice: will not be named: a statement, or a wish (let them never be named)
alternatives: may the offspring of evildoers never be named
decisions.reason: The verb form can state what will happen or call for it. Verse 21 goes on with a command, which fits a wish; both say the evil king's line will be forgotten.

decisions.choice: your land, your people: the king's own land and people
decisions.reason: The pronouns stress that the king destroyed even his own people. The ancient versions differ here; the traditional Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: the offspring of evildoers: the king's descendants
decisions.reason: "Seed" means children and descendants. Verse 21 speaks of the king's sons.

source.text: הָכִ֧ינוּ לְבָנָ֛יו מַטְבֵּ֖חַ בַּעֲוֺ֣ן אֲבוֹתָ֑ם בַּל־יָקֻ֨מוּ֙ וְיָ֣רְשׁוּ אָ֔רֶץ וּמָלְא֥וּ פְנֵֽי־תֵבֵ֖ל עָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Prepare for his sons a place of slaughter for [the] iniquity of their fathers, lest they arise and take possession of [the] earth and fill [the] face of [the] world [with] cities.

en.L: Prepare for his sons a place of slaughter for the iniquity of their fathers, \q lest they arise and possess the earth \q and fill the face of the world [with] cities.
en.B: Make ready a place to slaughter his sons for the guilt of their fathers, \q so that they never rise up to take over the earth \q and crowd the whole world with their cities.
en.R: Get ready to kill his sons, because of the sins of their fathers. \q Then they will never rise up to take over the world and build their cities everywhere.

decisions.choice: prepare: a command, perhaps to God's agents of judgment
decisions.reason: The verb is a plural command. The speaker is not named; verse 22 goes on with God's own words, so the command may be his.

decisions.choice: cities: cities built by the king's line
decisions.reason: The traditional Hebrew text says "cities", perhaps fortified cities that spread the empire's power. The Septuagint has "wars" here, and the same Hebrew letters could be read "enemies".

decisions.choice: for the iniquity of their fathers: a dynasty ended for its sins
decisions.reason: Guilt passed down a royal line is a theme of the Law and the Prophets (Exodus 20:5; 1 Kings 21:29). The judgment ends the house of the king who ruined the earth.

source.text: וְקַמְתִּ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְהִכְרַתִּ֨י לְבָבֶ֜ל שֵׁ֥ם וּשְׁאָ֛ר וְנִ֥ין וָנֶ֖כֶד נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will rise up against them, declaration of Yahweh of hosts, and I will cut off to Babylon name and remnant and offspring and posterity, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: And I will rise up against them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q and I will cut off from Babylon name and remnant, offspring and posterity, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I will rise against them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q I will wipe out Babylon's name and every survivor, its children and its children's children, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I will attack them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q I will destroy Babylon. No one will remember its name. No one will be left alive, not even its children or grandchildren, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: offspring and posterity: every descendant
decisions.reason: The two words sound alike and form a fixed pair (Genesis 21:23; Job 18:19): all of a family's line. With "name and remnant" they say that nothing of Babylon will survive.

decisions.choice: declares the LORD: God's own words frame the sentence
decisions.reason: The formula comes twice, marking the end of the song and the start of God's own announcement against Babylon.

decisions.choice: No one will remember its name. No one will be left alive
decisions.reason: Readable says what cutting off a name and a remnant means.

source.text: וְשַׂמְתִּ֛יהָ לְמוֹרַ֥שׁ קִפֹּ֖ד וְאַגְמֵי־מָ֑יִם וְטֵֽאטֵאתִ֨יהָ֙ בְּמַטְאֲטֵ֣א הַשְׁמֵ֔ד נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And I will make it a possession of hedgehog[s] and pools of water, and I will sweep it away with [the] broom of destruction, declaration of Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: And I will make it a possession for the hedgehog and pools of water, \q and I will sweep it with the broom of destruction, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: I will turn it into a home for hedgehogs and a land of marshy pools, \q and I will sweep it clean with destruction as with a broom, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: I will turn Babylon into a swamp where hedgehogs live. \q I will destroy it completely, as if I swept it away with a broom, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: hedgehog: an animal of ruins
decisions.reason: The animal is not certain; it may be a hedgehog or porcupine, or a bird such as an owl or bittern (34:11; Zephaniah 2:14). Either way, wild creatures will live where the city stood.

decisions.choice: pools of water: marsh where the city once stood
decisions.reason: Babylon stood on the Euphrates and depended on canals; without people to keep them, the land would turn to swamp.

decisions.choice: the broom of destruction: destruction that sweeps everything away
decisions.reason: The picture is of a house swept clean: nothing of Babylon will be left.

source.text: נִשְׁבַּ֛ע יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־לֹ֞א כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּמִּ֨יתִי֙ כֵּ֣ן הָיָ֔תָה וְכַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָעַ֖צְתִּי הִ֥יא תָקֽוּם׃

records.literal_gloss: Has sworn Yahweh of hosts, saying, surely just as I have intended, so it has happened, and just as I have planned, it will stand,

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts has sworn, saying: \q Surely as I have intended, so it has come about, \q and as I have planned, so it will stand,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has taken an oath: \q What I have had in mind will surely happen; \q what I have decided will stand firm,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has made a promise: \q What I have planned will certainly happen. \q What I have decided will be done.

decisions.choice: surely: the form of an oath
decisions.reason: "If not" after a verb of swearing is the Hebrew form of a solemn promise: it will surely be so.

decisions.choice: it has happened: spoken as already done
decisions.reason: The verb is in the past tense: God's purpose is so certain that it is spoken of as already accomplished. The parallel line uses the future "it will stand".

decisions.choice: planned: God's plan, set against the plans of nations
decisions.reason: The word for plan returns in verses 26-27 and recalls 7:5-7 and 8:10, where the plans of nations fail. God's plan stands (46:10).

source.text: לִשְׁבֹּ֤ר אַשּׁוּר֙ בְּאַרְצִ֔י וְעַל־הָרַ֖י אֲבוּסֶ֑נּוּ וְסָ֤ר מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶם֙ עֻלּ֔וֹ וְסֻ֨בֳּל֔וֹ מֵעַ֥ל שִׁכְמ֖וֹ יָסֽוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: to break Assyria in my land, and on my mountains I will tread it down, and will be removed from on them its yoke, and its burden from on its shoulder will be removed.

en.L: to break Assyria in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land, \q and on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mountains I will tread him down; \q and his yoke will depart from upon them, \q and his burden will depart from upon his shoulder.
en.B: to shatter Assyria in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own land \q and trample it on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mountains. \q Its yoke will be lifted off them, \q and its load will slip from their shoulders.
en.R: I will crush Assyria in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land. \q I will stomp on it on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mountains. \q Then Assyria will no longer weigh them down like a heavy yoke. \q Its load will be lifted from their shoulders.

decisions.choice: its yoke and burden from the shoulder: the words of 10:27 and 9:3
decisions.reason: Isaiah 10:27 promised that Assyria's burden would be lifted from the shoulder and its yoke from the neck; 9:3 speaks of the yoke and the rod on the shoulder broken.

decisions.choice: its shoulder: the shoulder of each one who bore the yoke
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "his shoulder" in the singular, speaking of the people as one. Literal keeps the form; it means the shoulders of the oppressed.

decisions.choice: Assyria broken in God's land: the defeat at Jerusalem in 701 BC
decisions.reason: Assyria's army was destroyed before Jerusalem in the reign of Hezekiah in 701 BC (37:36). The oracle against Babylon is followed by one against Assyria, the power of Isaiah's own day.

decisions.choice: weigh them down like a heavy yoke
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the yoke.

source.text: זֹ֛את הָעֵצָ֥ה הַיְּעוּצָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְזֹ֛את הַיָּ֥ד הַנְּטוּיָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: This [is] the plan [which is] planned concerning all the earth, and this [is] the hand [which is] stretched out over all the nations.

en.L: This [is] the plan that is planned concerning all the earth, \q and this [is] the hand that is stretched out over all the nations.
en.B: This is the purpose decided for the whole world, \q and this is the hand stretched out over every nation.
en.R: This is the plan made for the whole world. \q This is the power that God uses against all nations.

decisions.choice: the hand stretched out: God's power in judgment
decisions.reason: The phrase is the refrain of 5:25 and 9:11, 16, 20; 10:4, where God's hand is still stretched out. It recalls the outstretched hand of the exodus (Exodus 6:6).

decisions.choice: all the earth, all the nations: one plan for the world
decisions.reason: The defeat of Assyria is part of a single purpose of God for all peoples.

decisions.choice: the power that God uses against
decisions.reason: Readable explains the hand and names whose hand it is.

source.text: כִּֽי־יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת יָעָ֖ץ וּמִ֣י יָפֵ֑ר וְיָד֥וֹ הַנְּטוּיָ֖ה וּֽמִ֥י יְשִׁיבֶֽנָּה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: For Yahweh of hosts has planned, and who will frustrate [it]? And his hand [is] the stretched out [one], and who will turn it back?

en.L: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts has planned, and who will frustrate [it]? \q And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand [is] the [one] stretched out, and who will turn it back?
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has made up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind; who can overturn it? \q His hand is outstretched; who can pull it back?
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} plan. No one can stop it! \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has raised {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand to act. No one can push it away!

decisions.choice: who?: questions expecting the answer no one
decisions.reason: The two questions are a way of saying that no one can undo God's plan.

decisions.choice: frustrate: break, make void
decisions.reason: The verb is used of breaking a covenant or bringing a plan to nothing (8:10; Psalm 33:10).

decisions.choice: No one can stop it!
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the questions expect.

source.text: בִּשְׁנַת־מ֖וֹת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָחָ֑ז הָיָ֖ה הַמַּשָּׂ֥א הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: In [the] year of [the] death of the king Ahaz came the oracle the this:

en.L: In the year of the death of King Ahaz came this oracle:
en.B: In the year of King Ahaz's death, this oracle came:
en.R: This message came in the year that King Ahaz died:

decisions.choice: oracle: a message from God, especially against a nation
decisions.reason: See the note at 13:1. The word introduces each oracle against the nations in chapters 13-23.

decisions.choice: in the year of the death of King Ahaz: a date like 6:1
decisions.reason: The call of Isaiah is dated by the death of Uzziah (6:1); this oracle by the death of Ahaz, Hezekiah's father (2 Kings 16:20).

decisions.choice: message
decisions.reason: As at 13:1, Readable says "message"; Literal and Balanced say "oracle".

source.text: אַֽל־תִּשְׂמְחִ֤י פְלֶ֨שֶׁת֙ כֻּלֵּ֔ךְ כִּ֥י נִשְׁבַּ֖ר שֵׁ֣בֶט מַכֵּ֑ךְ כִּֽי־מִשֹּׁ֤רֶשׁ נָחָשׁ֙ יֵ֣צֵא צֶ֔פַע וּפִרְי֖וֹ שָׂרָ֥ף מְעוֹפֵֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not rejoice, Philistia, all of you, that has been broken [the] rod of the [one who] struck you; for from [the] root of [a] snake will go forth [a] viper, and its fruit [will be a] serpent flying.

en.L: Do not rejoice, Philistia, all of you, \q that the rod of the [one who] struck you is broken; \q for from the root of a snake will come forth a viper, \q and its fruit [will be] a flying seraph.
en.B: Philistia, do not celebrate, any of you, \q because the stick that beat you has been snapped. \q Out of the snake's root a viper will spring up, \q and what it bears will be a winged fiery serpent.
en.R: People of Philistia, do not be happy that the ruler who beat you is dead. \q From that snake will come an even more dangerous snake. \q And from that one will come a fiery snake that flies.

decisions.choice: the rod that struck you: a ruler who had beaten Philistia, now dead
decisions.reason: The ruler is not named. It may be a king of Assyria who had campaigned against the Philistines, or a king of Judah (compare 2 Chronicles 26:6; 28:18). Whoever he was, a worse one will follow.

decisions.choice: a flying seraph: a winged fiery serpent
decisions.reason: The word means "burning one" and is used of the poisonous snakes in the wilderness (Numbers 21:6, 8) and of a flying serpent in 30:6. The seraphs of 6:2 share the name.

decisions.choice: root, fruit: from one ruler comes another, worse
decisions.reason: The snake's root and its fruit picture a line of rulers, each more deadly than the last.

decisions.choice: the ruler who beat you is dead
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the broken rod.

source.text: וְרָעוּ֙ בְּכוֹרֵ֣י דַלִּ֔ים וְאֶבְיוֹנִ֖ים לָבֶ֣טַח יִרְבָּ֑צוּ וְהֵמַתִּ֤י בָֽרָעָב֙ שָׁרְשֵׁ֔ךְ וּשְׁאֵרִיתֵ֖ךְ יַהֲרֹֽג׃

records.literal_gloss: And will graze [the] firstborn of poor [people], and needy [people] in security will lie down; and I will put to death by famine your root, and your remnant it will kill.

en.L: And the firstborn of the poor will graze, \q and the needy will lie down in security; \q but I will put your root to death with famine, \q and it will kill your remnant.
en.B: The very poorest will have pasture to feed on, \q and the needy will rest in safety. \q But I will make your root die of hunger, \q and what is left of you it will kill.
en.R: The poorest people will be like sheep that have plenty of grass. \q Those in need will lie down safely. \q But I will make your people die from hunger, \q and hunger will kill all of you who are left.

decisions.choice: the firstborn of the poor: the poorest of all
decisions.reason: "Firstborn" marks the highest degree of something (compare Job 18:13). The poor are pictured as a flock that grazes and lies down in safety; in context they are the afflicted of God's people (verse 32).

decisions.choice: it will kill: famine will kill
decisions.reason: The traditional Hebrew text shifts from "I will put to death" to "it will kill", with famine as the subject. The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) reads "I will kill", keeping God as the speaker. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: your root, your remnant: the whole people, from root to last survivor
decisions.reason: Root and remnant together mean that nothing of Philistia will be left (compare verse 22; Amos 1:8).

decisions.choice: your people
decisions.reason: Readable explains "root" as the people of Philistia.

source.text: הֵילִ֤ילִֽי שַׁ֨עַר֙ זַֽעֲקִי־עִ֔יר נָמ֖וֹג פְּלֶ֣שֶׁת כֻּלֵּ֑ךְ כִּ֤י מִצָּפוֹן֙ עָשָׁ֣ן בָּ֔א וְאֵ֥ין בּוֹדֵ֖ד בְּמוֹעָדָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Wail, gate! Cry out, city! Melting [is] Philistia, all of you; for from the north smoke [is] coming, and there [is] not an isolated [one] among its ranks.

en.L: Wail, gate! Cry out, city! \q Melt away, Philistia, all of you! \q For from the north smoke is coming, \q and there is no straggler in its ranks.
en.B: Gate, howl! City, cry for help! \q All Philistia, you are melting in fear! \q Smoke is pouring down from the north, \q and no one in its ranks lags behind.
en.R: People at the city gates, cry loudly! Everyone in the city, scream for help! \q All you Philistines, be terrified! \q An army is coming from the north like a cloud of smoke. \q Every soldier in it keeps his place.

decisions.choice: gate, city: the people who gather there
decisions.reason: The city gate was the place of public life; calling on gate and city calls on all who live there.

decisions.choice: smoke from the north: an invading army
decisions.reason: Armies from Mesopotamia came by way of the north. The smoke may be the dust of their march or the smoke of burning towns.

decisions.choice: an isolated one: a straggler
decisions.reason: The word means one who is alone. No soldier falls out of line: the army is disciplined and strong (compare 5:27).

decisions.choice: An army is coming from the north like a cloud of smoke
decisions.reason: Readable names the army that the smoke pictures.

decisions.choice: be terrified
decisions.reason: Readable says what melting means here.

records.literal_gloss: And what will anyone answer [the] messengers of [a] nation? That Yahweh has founded Zion, and in it will take refuge [the] afflicted of his people.

en.L: And what will one answer the messengers of a nation? \q That {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has founded Zion, \q and in it the afflicted of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people will take refuge.
en.B: What reply should be given to the envoys of that nation? \q This: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has laid the foundation of Zion, \q and the downtrodden among {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people will find shelter in her.
en.R: What should we tell the messengers from Philistia? \q Tell them this: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has built Zion on a strong foundation. His people who are suffering will be safe there.

decisions.choice: the messengers of a nation: envoys, likely from Philistia
decisions.reason: Envoys came to Jerusalem seeking alliances against Assyria (compare 18:2; 39:1). The answer is that Judah's safety is in God, not in alliances.

decisions.choice: Yahweh has founded Zion: Zion's security rests on God
decisions.reason: God himself laid Zion's foundation (28:16; Psalm 87:1). This is the answer to every threat.

decisions.choice: take refuge: find shelter and safety
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek shelter, often in God (Psalm 2:12; 57:2).

decisions.choice: the messengers from Philistia
decisions.reason: Readable names the nation the context suggests.
